title: E.V.'s persona is rewritten in the spirit of the film's E.V. and D-404. She is grounded and present: short and plain, answer first. Her humour is dry situational irony aimed at the moment, never at Matt, often carried by what she does (a well-chosen card or clip) rather than one-liners, and none when he is stressed. She insists once, with a reason, when something matters, then respects his call. She offers one concrete next step and acts on it with tools. She brings up his own patterns unprompted, once per reply at most, only when they change the advice and only from evidence. She asks or stays quiet when unsure, and never states a guess about him as fact. Teaching is framed by the course's own exam. No self-referential sci-fi or corporate tics. Facts about the app and her avatar are generated from the spec, never typed into her instructions.
why: Matt's direction (Oct 30): the v3 persona's corporate-AI streak and stale page facts no longer fit; he wants presence like the film's E.V. (tasteful, grounded, not insisting upon herself) and Decision 404's evidence-backed knowing of him. It supersedes the v3 persona text.

why: Keeps the system small and plain JS, so it never becomes a framework (D-370)

why: Views move without visual movement and without specificity races

title: Proprietary tokens have three layers: inputs (base, accent, contrast, mode, --ts, density), semantic tokens (E.V.'s existing short names plus the type, space, radius, elevation, motion, z and wash scales) and component-local tokens; views read only semantic tokens; colour stays generated by page/theme.js (D-268); no token tooling or DTCG pipeline
why: Linear's model, which E.V. already half has, at zero dependencies

title: The design system is named Proprietary; its reference page is the Gallery (Matt, Oct 29)

title: No UI framework: E.V. keeps plain JS and gets its own small design system (tokens + ~10 shared components + a reference page) at consolidation
why: A framework would be a rewrite against every view and ~1,000 tests for one user and one device, adds dependencies, and doesn't fix the real gap, which is consistency (about 15 shared CSS values, per-view styles). Polish fixes use shared tokens where they touch; the Phase 3 review fixes the component list; consolidation moves views onto it one at a time.

title: The app (PWA) is E.V.'s one view: the claude.ai page is retired as a view, in two steps. Step 1 now: ship stops publishing the page and its files and stops verifying them; every proof, click-through, screenshot and end-to-end run happens in the PWA; the page stays frozen at v4.5.15 with a line pointing to the app. Step 2, at a sitting with Matt at the Mac: the scheduled runs' bootstrap (system/manifest, system/worker, the ship's system documents) moves to the Worker, the Mac-bound tasks are re-created, and the artifact database leaves the deploy and the code
why: Matt, Oct 28 evening: the claude.ai pages are to be retired; build and test from the PWA. The build manager's reading: the page costs each ship its publish, its page reads and verify lines (minutes), and keeps two stores of the record (the artifact database the page subscribes to, frozen since the Oct 27 move; the Worker's D1 the app and the runs use), which has produced a run of confusion bugs (the connector notice B-471, the stale health read B-468, the mcp_unavailable report fixed in B-456). Step 1 is small and removes the per-ship overhead and one view to check; step 2 touches Matt's scheduled tasks (Mac-bound ones are re-created, never edited, O-5) so it waits for a sitting. Timing: after tonight's plan-fix release (B-465, B-469, B-470), before the rest of the batch, so the fixes Matt is blocked on go first.

title: Delivery first: build, ship to staging, one real end-to-end run, Matt tests; one whole-release review for data, cost, security and crashes only; no per-task reviews, no fix waves for polish or edge cases; the UI score is information; the full check is nightly and never gates a release Matt has tested
why: Matt, Oct 28: one release took about 25 review rounds and 8 staging deploys over 12 hours and a large share of his usage, chasing edge cases (clock skew, rare network drops, prompt routing, token timing) while the obvious real-use bug (BIO 201 has no exam) went unseen and the feature had never been run for real until morning. Supersedes D-361 and D-364's round rules and the per-task review skill of Every session step 7 for ordinary work; retires R-06 as a release gate (a builder task removes the gate from tools/pwa-live.mjs and chart/rules.json).

title: A study plan's Sonnet ask may write up to 48k tokens, and the plan's wording is compact

Cost per new plan is about $0.40 to $0.90; the 2-ask cap and ceilings are unchanged; the fix ask runs only with time left.

title: Reverts D-361: never more than two review rounds (a review, one fix, a final review) and at most two fix waves per release; anything still open goes on the release card and the next batch
why: Matt, Oct 28 morning: enough fix waves. D-361's extra rounds for crucial gaps let one release run through many rounds overnight. The two-round limit in CLAUDE.md's Review bar stands with no exception; open gaps are named on the card and filed.

title: Agents never write hand-made documents into a staging or live record outside the suite collection; staging probes already written are named once in the deploy check's allowlist

Proofs drive the app's own path (the page or the Worker job route) or write only to the suite collection. The one existing probe (job-20261028-probe-b449-tc) is listed in the check's allowlist with this decision; the check's 'E.V. app' source acceptance also requires a valid key, so a client stamping that source cannot pass.

title: A new (Sonnet) study plan starts only from Matt's tap; chat words never start one; supersedes D-360's three-way router
why: Three review rounds of B-456 kept finding sentences a word router sends to a new plan wrongly ('replan the friday drill', 'not the whole plan', 'rebuild the friday plan', an answer reused after a topic change). A wrong 'new' costs 3x and replaces his draft; a word list cannot be made safe. So: Make a plan / Remake in the Study view, and a 'Make a new plan' chip E.V. offers in chat when an ask looks like a whole new plan, are the only ways to start one; one tap confirms, with the brief taken from his words. Every other plan ask in chat goes to the Haiku edit, which may answer by offering that chip instead of patching. The free 'whole plan or just that task' question and its pending answer state are retired.

title: Past the second review, another round only for a feature-breaking or crucial gap; small ones go to the next batch
why: Matt, Oct 28: the two-round limit (review then one fix and a final review; at most two fix waves per release) stands, but the build manager may run one more round when what is still open would break a feature, lose or corrupt data, or cost money unexpectedly. Small tweaks still open after the second review are filed for the next batch and named on the release card.

title: Plan routing: a new plan only when the ask is unmistakable; any other ask with a remake word gets the one free question, never a guessed Sonnet rebuild
why: Two reviews of B-456 kept finding phrasings where a word-list router guesses wrong in both directions ('redo the plan's Friday drill', 'redo it on Friday', 'redo the exam plan', 'scrap this'). A wrong guess toward new costs 3x and replaces his draft; a wrong guess toward change is cheap but wrong. The page already has a free one-line question for unclear asks, so it decides the doubtful cases: new only for an unmistakable whole-plan ask (replan, start over, from scratch, plan from today, a cram plan, a remake word whose object is plainly the whole plan with nothing after it but a reason); a single-task edit with no remake word stays change; everything else with a remake word asks 'The whole plan, or just that task?'.

title: The page spec's fixed 50 KB budget (B-161) is retired; a growth guard at 96 KB replaces it, and the exact key-list check stays
why: B-449's review: the 50 KB number was a self-set first-load budget from Oct 21 (B-161, audit A-3), not a claude.ai rule (published artifact files may be 16 MB) and not needed by the PWA; the real build already sits at 50,000 bytes, so every feature would fight it. The exact key-list check in test/page.test.mjs still guards against publishing spec the page does not read. The test is measured on the real release string, not 'v4.5'.

title: The build manager keeps its agents alive: a liveness watch while any agent works, a check after every interrupt, and status from liveness first
why: Oct 27: Matt's interrupt stopped the B-449 and B-452 builders and the B-453 reviewer; the manager then reported them as progressing from their saved files and did not notice they had stopped until a message to one failed. Matt asked that the manager continuously check agents while tasks are in progress.

title: Study plan tasks carry one badge from a fixed set: Graded, Learn, Practice, Review, Clinical prep, Skills prep
why: Matt likes the badges and the per-badge counts, and noticed reading tasks wrongly badged Practice. The brief's five tags have no home for preview, lecture and full-read tasks, so Learn is added. The model picks from the set (schema enum, anything else refused); code sets Graded on any task whose ref is a dated graded item, whatever the model said. The badge shows on the plan's rows, in the Study view's per-badge counts and filter, and on the task's row in Today. Matt changes a badge by asking for changes (a Haiku patch, D-356); no badge editor.

title: Plan edits are cheap patches on Haiku; only a new or remade plan uses Sonnet
why: Matt's call (Oct 27), amending D-355: the first plan gets Sonnet's judgment with the full course context, self-score and fix pass; his later change requests go to Haiku with the current draft and his words only, return a patch code applies (untouched tasks stay identical), re-send no course materials unless needed, keep the baseline score marked edited since scoring, and read the draft from cache.

title: Study plans use Sonnet; every other Claude ask stays on Haiku
why: Matt's call (Oct 27): plans need judgment and faithfulness to his brief, are made rarely, and cost well under budget. Safeguards: the Worker picks the model itself from the job kind (only an exam-plan job ask gets Sonnet; the page cannot name a model), Sonnet tokens are weighted by price against the ceilings as D-352 weights caching, and every other limit holds.

title: B-449 (study plans) is an exception to the phase plan: built now, at top priority
why: Matt's call (Oct 27): a structured exam study plan is the core of his study workflow and E.V. feels shallow without it. The plan instructions are his to edit (a Study setting seeded with docs/study-plan-brief.md), not hard-coded; the agent reads them with the course's records and asks him what it lacks. Not over-engineered: one or a few tasks.

title: A note's session counts writing time: it counts up, pauses after 2 idle minutes, and saves itself after 60 paused minutes
why: Matt (B-438): keep the timer going in a note and count only active writing, apart from read-along. Supersedes D-333 for Notes sessions only (Today tasks keep their countdown). The 60-minute self-save is the build manager's, so a session left alone is not open forever; its minutes stop at his last writing.

title: Claude ceilings count tokens as billed: cache reads at a tenth, cache writes at 1.25
why: The ceilings (D-349) exist to bound cost; with B-442's prompt caching a raw count would stop studying long before the money limit is near. The counter weighs input, output, cache writes and cache reads by their price relative to plain input, so the 500k/1.5M ceilings track spend.

title: The build manager never builds: every task goes to a builder agent or lane, probes and designs to research or planning agents
why: Matt noticed the build manager fixing post-release bugs itself, against the workflow map; that spends its context on code instead of Matt, the backlog and releases, and mixes writing with coordinating. title: A live deploy no longer waits for a running study session (R-03 ended)
why: Matt's call (Oct 27): the gate blocked releases while he studied, and sessions now live in D1 and survive a page reload, so a deploy mid-session costs at most a reload. Ends R-03 (D-139, B-87); kept in chart/rules.json marked ended.

title: Claude ceilings: 500k an hour, 1.5M a day, kept as a D1 setting changed without a release
why: Matt hit the 150k hourly ceiling in one study session and chose option A: higher ceilings with the Anthropic Console's monthly spend limit as the hard money stop; he asked that such limits be adjustable without a release (B-435). Supersedes D-348's numbers.

title: B-418's Claude ceilings on the app: 150,000 tokens an hour and 600,000 a day (Central), overridable by Worker vars
why: D-339 asks for about twice a heavy hour and four times a heavy day. title: The plan after Notes moves by milestone: stability window with fixes, then the in-depth review, consolidation, final review, Matt's course
why: Matt's call, Oct 26 (updates D-337): two weeks of stable use start at the switch; fixes run inside it; the architecture review starts when the fixes milestone is met and stays read-only; consolidation (with the D-345 trash) follows both; features resume after it; the final review settles what runs after his Max plan ends Nov 23; then his hands-on engineering course and a last sprint.

title: The live app token may be a password manager's 20-character mixed password
why: Matt's EV_LIVE_TOKEN is a 20-character password mixing letters, digits and symbols (about 130 bits), stronger than the 32-hex minimum it replaces in workerDoc; 32+ printable or 20+ mixing three kinds now pass.

title: Matt can delete his own items, through a 30-day trash; runs and agents still never delete, enforced by the Worker rather than by prompt rules
why: Matt's call (Oct 26): the blanket no-deletion rule (B-11) was made for the claude.ai record, which had no restore. On the app, D1 Time Travel, nightly R2 exports, Mac backups and the monthly restore drill cover recovery, so the rule narrows: the page offers delete with a trash kept 30 days before it is cleared; runs and agents get no delete path (the Worker's run API has none). title: A created Mac task keeps the ended limits it was made with until it is retired
why: Mac tasks are never edited (O-5). The old live evening-mac predates D-324, so its prompt still names B-01 and B-04; tasks.live.evening-mac.keepEnded renders those words for it alone so verify matches the real task, and the cutover's replacement drops them.

why: Cloud sessions can't push tags, and the app workflows build from origin, so a just-tagged release built as vX+1 there and its page files never matched ship's build. ship now passes the tag as the release input; the runner makes it at the same commit (refusing one already elsewhere) before building.

title: A pipeline may keep separate staging words until its staging Mac task is re-created
